title: LMCache/LMCache v0.5.0
event_hint: LMCache v0.5.0 release: adds Peer-to-Peer (P2P) KV cache transfer between LMCache instances in multiprocess (MP) mode, plus CacheBlend, prefetch sliding-window, asymmetric serde, and new L2 backends/connectors.
problem: KV cache reuse across multiple LMCache serving instances previously required indirect paths; MP-mode deployments needed a way to look up and transfer KV cache directly between instances, and existing transfer/prefetch/serde mechanisms lacked the flexibility (asymmetric precision, sliding-window prefetch, segmented-prefix retrieval) for efficient distributed reuse.
mechanism: v0.5.0 introduces a P2P adapter and transfer-channel abstraction for MP mode, with a new RPC interface for P2P lookup and lock, enabling direct KV cache lookup and transfer between LMCache instances. The MP coordinator gains P2P info and runtime registration/deregistration of L2 adapters. Supporting features: asymmetric serde (e.g., FP16 Key with FP8 Value), Device-DAX hybrid L1 overflow, DeviceIPCWrapper for device-agnostic KV-cache IPC, CacheBlend segmented-prefix retrieval with coordinator knobs and observability span (cb.coordinator_match), prefetch sliding window (1/N) with a blocking WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS to avoid busy-polling, and new backends/connectors (SGLang XPU, native Aerospike L2, MUSA stage-2).

evidence.claim: v0.5.0 introduces full P2P support for multiprocess (MP) mode: a P2P adapter (#3740), transfer-channel abstraction for MP mode (#3712), a new RPC interface for P2P lookup and lock (#3728), P2P info into the MP coordinator (#3706), and runtime registration/deregistration of L2 adapters (#3743).
evidence.baseline: prior LMCache releases (no direct P2P transfer)
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: Peer-to-Peer (P2P) KV Cache Transfer

evidence.claim: CacheBlend additions: fault-inject L2 adapter + segmented-prefix retrieval path (#3697), coordinator knobs exposed as CLI flags (#3731), global CacheBlend token matching optimization (#3708), and an observability span cb.coordinator_match (#3711).
Asymmetric serde support is added (e.g., FP16 Key with FP8 Value) (#3277), enabling different precisions for K and V in MP mode.
Prefetch & Performance: a blocking WAIT_PREFETCH_STATUS avoids busy-polling the lookup wait (#3704), and a prefetch sliding window (1/N) adds bitmap operations (#3745).

New backends/connectors: SGLang XPU connectors for KV cache transfer (#3121), optional native Aerospike L2 backend via BUILD_AEROSPIKE (#3458), Stage-2 MUSA support with optional native in-process transfer (#3580), nixl_storage presence_cache_only option (#3587); plus multi-LMCache-server deployment with vLLM (#3248).
evidence.value: SGLang XPU; Aerospike L2; MUSA; multi-server vLLM
evidence.source_locator: Evidence locator: Backends & Connectors; Multiprocess (MP) Mode

evaluation_context: GitHub release notes (LMCache v0.5.0, published 2026-06-23, full changelog v0.4.7...v0.5.0). The evidence is a feature/release-notes enumeration referencing PR numbers; it describes mechanisms and integrations (vLLM, SGLang) but contains no quantitative benchmarks - no WAN RTT, transferred bytes, cache hit rate, P95 latency, compression ratio, or consistency overhead numbers are present.
limitations: This is a software release notes source, not a benchmark study. No quantitative performance, hit-rate, transfer-volume, or latency measurements are included in the visible evidence; all claims are feature descriptions tied to PR numbers. Cross-region/WAN behavior is not characterized - P2P transfer is between LMCache instances (MP mode) and the evidence does not specify whether it targets local fabric, rack, or WAN. Worker-adapter liveness hygiene is introduced in two parts but its measured effect is not quantified.
project_relevance: LMCache v0.5.0 is directly relevant to the cross-region/KVCache-transfer topic: P2P KV cache transfer, CacheBlend segmented-prefix reuse, prefetch sliding window, and asymmetric serde are concrete mechanisms for distributed KV-cache movement and placement. For the project card it is a release (engineering artifact) confirming capability exists, but it provides no quantitative WAN RTT/hit-rate/P95 evidence to judge cross-region deployment value; it is better suited to the KVCache-ecosystem radar than to a deep quantitative briefing.
